excerpt: Most of the working material here is small. Two or three Latin words, a psalm, an hour of the day.

title: The Two Hidden Pillars
excerpt: Every diagram of the Tree of Life shows three vertical pillars — Mercy on the right, Severity on the left, and the Golden or Middle Pillar down the centre.

title: The Two Inclinations Must Be Balanced
excerpt: There's a moment in a relationship that everyone recognises and almost nobody can date.

title: The Uses and Types of Chalices
excerpt: Read the table and there are eight chalices, each with its own name and its own blessed liquid.

title: The Uses and Types of Pentacles
excerpt: Three of the four weapons work the same way. Own one cup, one sword, one wand, charge whichever aspect you need today, and the same object serves for everything.

title: The Uses and Types of Swords
excerpt: There is a moment in any dealing with something powerful where the question stops being what do I want and becomes why should it listen to me.

title: The Uses and Types of Wands
excerpt: Four weapons sit on the table. Three of them are optional on any given day.

title: The Voice of Ceremony
excerpt: A wedding, a funeral, a harvest festival. There are people standing in the room, and the words are said out loud so they can hear them.

title: The Voice of Magic
excerpt: The words are printed. Anybody can read them off the page. So what is left to get wrong?

title: The Voice of Prayer
excerpt: Three of the four voices in this practice are for getting something done.

title: The Voice of Ritual
excerpt: Both are formulas, said out loud, often with other people in the room.

title: The Wand Carries All Four Worlds
excerpt: The chalice is water, the sword is air, the pentacle is earth. Each does its element's work, and reaching outside it means reaching for a different tool.

title: The Water Vase
excerpt: Somebody has told you something and you do not believe it. You do not own a scrying ball, or you do and it is under linen halfway through its eleven days.

title: The Wheel Is the Oath
excerpt: Everybody knows the wheel image. Life goes round, you are on it, and the usual advice is to stop clinging or stop wanting and it will let you go.

title: The Wizardly Trades
excerpt: Nobody can study everything. The Octovium alone is eight full disciplines in original editions, the ten schools each have eight degrees, and there are seventy more schools after that.

title: The Yoga of Kabbalah
excerpt: Most people picture Kabbalah as a diagram. Ten circles, twenty-two paths, and a lot of contemplating them.

title: There Is No Hidden Sefirah Called Da'at
excerpt: Look at almost any modern Tree of Life and there's an eleventh circle on it, drawn with a broken line, sitting in the gap below the top three.

title: Thirty-Two Universal Laws, and How to Nullify One
excerpt: Everything in creation, formation and manifestation is governed by a law, or rather by groups of laws.

title: This Moment Is My Whole Life
excerpt: Ask somebody that and watch what they do. They work it out. Forty-one so far, family history is decent, so maybe another forty.

title: Three and the Act of Synthesis
excerpt: A project that will not start. A conversation that has gone flat. A room that feels dead.

title: Three Attributes Oversee the Ten
excerpt: The number ten arrived from somewhere older, and that settles the count.

title: Tin and the Jupiter Set
excerpt: Most of the working material in this curriculum aims at something specific.

title: Two Incantations Carry Everything
excerpt: A reader working through this material meets dozens of named incantations.

title: Two Power Supplies and a Gearbox
excerpt: From two places, and they don't mix on their own. Three of the sphere's rings run on you.

title: Tzimtzum Is Contraction and Expansion at Once
excerpt: Every system that starts with one undifferentiated thing has the same problem at step two.

title: We Are Not Punished for Our Sins, But By Them
excerpt: Most people who leave a religion keep one piece of its furniture without noticing.

title: What the Drills Ask of the Senses
excerpt: Go through every exercise in this curriculum and ask what the practitioner is actually asked to do with their attention.

title: What the System Says It Cannot Do
excerpt: Buried in the spellbook, attached to a charm for calming animals, is one of the strangest sentences in the whole curriculum.

title: Why a Pentacle Is Written On
excerpt: The chalice holds liquid, the sword has an edge, the wand is a length of wood.

title: Why Ten and Not Nine
excerpt: Every diagram of this tradition has ten circles on it. Ask why ten and most people can't tell you, including people who have been drawing it for years.

title: Why the Source Needs a First God
excerpt: Later on you get spells. Every one of them has you say a name out loud — an angel's name, a name of God, one of the ten stations on the Tree of Life.

title: You Are Driving by the Rear Window
excerpt: Ask somebody what they are certain of and they will tell you something that already happened.

title: You Cannot Experience It, You Must Be It
excerpt: Every tradition has the same embarrassment. Somebody reaches the thing everybody is aiming at, comes back, and cannot say anything useful about it.

title: You Must Know Your Alef From Your Bet
excerpt: A Persian turns up at the house of a wise teacher named Yehudah and asks to be taught Hebrew.

title: Zacuto and the Hebrew Grimoire
excerpt: Anyone who reads around Western magic knows the famous books. The Key of Solomon, the Lesser Key, Abramelin with its Divine Names and magic squares and its long preparation.

title: Authentic Kabbalah — Map of Content
excerpt: What Kabbalah is, when it actually started, and how to read a tradition whose own vocabulary has been borrowed, mislabelled and sold — built from Jacobus Swart's forty-year teaching syllabus.
